newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Apr jet/gas oil trades - 80cts.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Apr jet/gas oil trades - 80cts.

text.p: Singapore April jet fuel/gas oil regrade extended its early day fall to trade late afternoon on Wednesday at minus 80 cents as the market came under strong selling pressure on reduced demand, traders said.
"The regrade is coming off sharply, there are alot of sellers out there," one broker said.
April regrade was last quoted at -95/-70 cents from Tuesday's -60/-40 cents, brokers said. They said the market traded to a low of -65 cents late last night.
This afternoon's selling pressure was partly blamed on news of the low offers going into two purchase tenders.
Sources said the Taiwan tender to buy 32,000-tonnes of jet fuel for May 15-30 delivery was at awarded at $203 per tonne cost-and-freight basis, down about $10 from its previous monthly purchase.
Nepal received an offer of $204 per tonne for its tender to buy 30,000-tonnes of kerosene for May delivery, down almost $30 from its previous awarded for March delivery cargoes.

Lower prices were also seen in the Singapore physical market, late Tuesday, where jet fuel was offered down to a low of $25.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for a 100,000-barrel cargo loading April 25-30.
Traditionally, jet fuel value slips below gas oil in the second quarter as demand reaches a low as jet-kerosene is no longer needed as a winter heating fuel.
Traders said the sharply lower regrade numbers are also due to sustained support for prompt gas oil in the physical market which is also keeping gas oil swaps firm.
April gas oil was last quoted at $26.70/$26.85 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $26.30/$26.40, brokers said.
They said deals were done earlier in the day at $26.65 and $26.68 per barrel.
Traders said the latest hike was partly due to market perception that local trader Hin Leong will continue to buy physical gas oil for at least another few days.
